findings.what: Symmetry tau (SAFE_DIV_SISTER_SYMMETRY_TAU 0.6 -> 0.65..1.0) is the largest division lever in the 6bba lab, but it is EMBRYO-SPECIFIC and fails the both-embryo test. Do not ladder it and do not put it in a final. exp60 6bba (ctl): tau 0.65 +0.00121, 0.7 +0.00310, 0.75 +0.00498, 0.8 +0.00478, 0.9 +0.00705, 1.0 +0.00628. Both halves are positive at every value (0.75: SELECTION +0.00516, CONFIRMATION +0.00482; div 15/17/73 -> 21/21/67, i.e. +6 TP / +4 FP among +161 forks; clip bootstrap P(<0) 0.004). But on 44b6 exp64-71: 0.7 -0.00051, 0.75 -0.00086 (ins -0.00122; 0 TP / +4 FP among +289 forks; 54 new clips -0.00169; leak-group bootstrap P(<0) 0.99), 0.8 -0.00106, 0.9 -0.00165. On exp60 44b6-17 it has no evaluable effect up to 0.8, and at 0.9 the first FP appears. Mechanism: extra asymmetric forks match GT only where annotated divisions are dense (6bba 5.2% vs 44b6 0.79% of predicted nodes annotated). The public embryo's type is unknown, so the public sign is a coin flip on embryo type, and the private embryos (~71%) could be either. This is the likely shape of a PP-only public jump like Justin CH123's (70 subs; x138's dormant validator sweeps exactly these PP keys, from a 'public 0.939' base config), i.e. public-embryo fitting.
